slots.practicalActivity: If you have access to a Purview tenant (a trial account works), sign into the Purview governance portal and click through its main left-nav areas (Data Map, Data Catalog, Insights, Management). If you don't have access, sketch the portal's main areas from the lesson and write one sentence on what each area is for.
slots.deliverable: A short written map of the Purview portal's main areas and what each one is for.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short note on which Purview roles (Data Source Admin, Data Reader, Data Curator, Collection Admin, etc.) a real organization's data map admin, a data steward, and a read-only business analyst would each need, and at what scope (root collection vs. a specific collection).
slots.deliverable: A role-to-person mapping noting which Purview role and scope fits three different real job functions.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch a collection hierarchy for an organization with three departments (e.g., Finance, Sales, HR) -- a root collection and three child collections, with one sentence on what access each department's team should have at their own collection versus the root.
slots.deliverable: A sketched collection hierarchy with per-department access notes.

slots.practicalActivity: Register a source of your choice in Purview (a real Azure Blob Storage account if you have access, or walk through the Register sources dialog without completing it) and note every field the form asks for -- name, subscription, storage account, collection. Then find that source in both Map view and Table view and write down one thing each view makes easier to see.
slots.deliverable: A registered (or walked-through) data source with its required fields noted, plus one advantage each of Map view and Table view.

slots.practicalActivity: For the source you registered in the previous slot, configure (or sketch) a scan: choose a scan rule set, decide whether to use a system default or a custom rule set naming specific file types/classifications to look for, and write one sentence on why you chose that scope.
slots.deliverable: A configured or sketched scan with its scan rule set choice and one sentence justifying the scope.

slots.practicalActivity: Decide a recurring schedule (e.g., weekly) for the scan you configured and write why that cadence fits the source's rate of change. Then write a short troubleshooting checklist (credentials, network/firewall access, managed identity permissions) you'd walk through if that scan failed on its first run.
slots.deliverable: A chosen scan schedule with justification, plus a scan-failure troubleshooting checklist.

slots.practicalActivity: Data Map lab: walk the full pipeline end to end for one source -- register it, assign it to a collection, configure a scan rule set, run or schedule the scan, and view the resulting assets in both Map view and Table view. Write a short run log of each step and what you'd check if any step failed.
slots.deliverable: A step-by-step run log covering registration through scan execution for one real or simulated data source.

slots.practicalActivity: List three system classifications Purview would likely detect automatically in the source you registered earlier (SSN, email, credit card), and name one custom classification you'd need to write yourself for data specific to your organization (an internal employee ID format, for example) -- with the regex or pattern you'd use for it.
slots.deliverable: A list of three applicable system classifications plus one custom classification with its matching pattern.

slots.practicalActivity: Design a small sensitivity-label hierarchy (e.g., Public, General, Confidential, Highly Confidential) and assign one label to each classification you identified in the previous slot, then write one sentence on whether that label should auto-apply from a scan result or require manual review first.
slots.deliverable: A sensitivity-label hierarchy mapped to the classifications from the previous slot, with an auto-apply vs. manual-review decision for each.

lessons.title: The Purview Data Catalog and Unified Catalog Overview

slots.practicalActivity: Search the catalog for the source you scanned earlier (or, if unavailable, write the search terms and filters you'd use) and note which metadata fields actually help a business user decide whether an asset is the right one -- not just its name, but its description, classifications, and owner.
slots.deliverable: A list of the metadata fields that most help a non-technical user identify the right asset in a catalog search.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a glossary term definition for one ambiguous business term in your organization (e.g., "active customer"), precise enough that two teams can't disagree about it, then link it conceptually to one data asset and one data product it should attach to.
slots.deliverable: A written glossary term definition linked to a named data asset and data product.

slots.practicalActivity: Curate one asset from your scanned source: add a description, assign an owner/expert contact, attach the glossary term from the previous slot, and assign it to a business domain (Sales, Finance, HR, etc.). Write one sentence on why that domain fits.
slots.deliverable: One fully curated asset record (description, owner, glossary term, business domain) with reasoning for the domain choice.

lessons.title: Lineage From Azure Data Factory and Synapse

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a real or imagined table you've worked with. List three process steps that could move data out of it (a copy activity, a dataflow, a stored procedure) and name the downstream dataset each one points to, using Purview's dataset-node/process-node pattern. Then say which single column you'd most want to trace end-to-end through that lineage graph, and why.
slots.deliverable: A sketched lineage chain (dataset-process-dataset, three steps) for a real or imagined table, plus one column chosen for end-to-end tracing.

lessons.title: Lineage From Fabric and Power BI

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the lineage chain from the previous slot one more hop downstream into a Power BI dataset or report. Then write one sentence on a question a Data Estate Insights report would help answer that a single lineage diagram wouldn't (e.g., how much sensitive data sits unclassified across the whole estate).
slots.deliverable: A lineage chain extended into a Power BI asset, plus one question Data Estate Insights answers that lineage alone cannot.

slots.practicalActivity: Design a one-page governance dashboard outline: three metrics a governance lead would want to see weekly (e.g., percent of assets classified, number of open access requests, scan failure count), and for each, name which Purview Insights report would supply it.
slots.deliverable: A three-metric governance dashboard outline with the source Insights report named for each metric.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick the asset you curated earlier. Write out the self-service request flow a consumer would follow to get access to it: the justification text they'd type when clicking Request access, and what you'd expect an approver to want to see before moving the request from Pending to Approved and finally Completed.
slots.deliverable: A written access-request justification and approver expectations for one real asset, tracked through its four request states.

slots.practicalActivity: Write one data quality rule for the asset you've been curating (a completeness, uniqueness, or validity check) and the threshold that would trigger a failure. Then sketch a two-step approval workflow (steward review, then owner sign-off) for applying a new classification label at scale across a collection.
slots.deliverable: One written data quality rule with a failure threshold, plus a sketched two-step label-approval workflow.

slots.practicalActivity: Name one Purview compliance capability (eDiscovery, retention labels, communication compliance, insider risk management) that would matter most for an organization you know, and write two sentences on the specific compliance obligation it would help satisfy.
slots.deliverable: One named Purview compliance capability with two sentences on the obligation it addresses.

slots.practicalActivity: Following the lesson's enterprise rollout case study, write a phased rollout plan for an organization you know -- which business unit goes first, which sources get registered and scanned in phase one, and what success looks like before expanding. Then complete the course's own Purview Practice Lab exercise end-to-end.
slots.deliverable: A phased Purview rollout plan for a real or representative organization, plus the completed Purview Practice Lab exercise.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone review: assemble a one-page Purview governance plan for a real or realistic organization -- the collection hierarchy, one registered source with its scan schedule, the classification/sensitivity-label scheme, one curated asset with its glossary term and domain, the lineage chain you traced, and the access-policy flow a consumer would follow. Check it against the best-practices lesson's recommendations.
slots.deliverable: A one-page Purview governance plan covering collections, a registered/scanned source, classification, curation, lineage, and access policy, reviewed against best practices.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can register and scan a real data source in Microsoft Purview, apply classifications and sensitivity labels, curate catalog assets with glossary terms and business domains, trace and read lineage across a multi-hop pipeline, and run a self-service access-request workflow end to end -- the core Purview operating skills the path's Fabric governance course then extends into OneLake and Power BI.
